notes:
Summary: Mid-market B2B SaaS (workflows + knowledge bases) evaluating Redwood starting with Hosted API POC for reranking, then interested in Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation. Key ask: reranking endpoint + offline scoring so we can run large evals against production candidates.

Context / pain: search relevance drift after product docs growth; current stack = BM25 + small embed-based candidate rerank done in python microservice. Cost rising; latency spikes on peak. Want deterministic, testable rerank pipeline and simple way to run offline evals against candidate sets.

Technical requirements (from CT O/product):
- Workload: offline scoring (10k-50k eval examples/day), live rerank calls ~150-250 qps at peak (burst).
- Latency: p95 target <120ms for rerank endpoint; accept higher for batch/offline scoring.
- Throughput: consistent 200 qps sustained desired for peak features.
- Model preferences: open models first (Llama2 variants), likely 7B/13B quantized for Dedicated. Want Redwood's model catalog recommendations.
- Routing/fallback: need deterministic fallback to smaller model or BM25 when capacity constrained.
- Observability: per-route latency/cost breakdown, token-level cost estimates, trace for rerank calls.
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML), audit logs, customer-managed keys preferred, data residency: US-only for now.

Quote from CTO on 2026-02-09 call: "We need offline reproducibility — if the eval numbers move, we need to trace which model/params changed."

POC scope agreed: Hosted API -> Verify rerank endpoint behavior and streaming/structured responses; produce offline scoring artifacts (CSV of scores) and run Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization on our workload. Then price out Dedicated for sustained throughput and residency needs.

Notes on cost sensitivity: Product team expects to keep annual infra <$200k for inference; wants clear unit economics (cost per 1k rerank calls).

Stitch items: security questionnaire filled 60%, waiting on KMS integration details. Pricing deck reviewed (drive link). SE demo run 2026-01-22 (ff link).
